items.title: AI is giving writers the support publishing cannot
items.excerpt: Marian Stan argues AI can now give aspiring novelists the editorial feedback that traditional publishing has long failed to provide, framing AI as a manuscript-development aid rather than a ghostwriter.

items.title: Publishing Ireland conference: AI and rising costs high on the agenda
items.excerpt: Publishing Ireland's autumn conference tackled AI alongside rising costs across the book trade and how Irish regional content is faring.

items.title: Important Anthropic Settlement Update: Check Your Claim by Friday, November 20
items.excerpt: First payments from the Bartz v. Anthropic settlement are expected the week of November 23; they will be about 70 percent of what each author is owed, and claimants must check their claims by November 20.

items.title: Audible Audio Discovery: An AI Voice Beside the Narrator
items.excerpt: Narrator-side view of Audible's audio discovery previews, which pair a human narrator's sample with an overview read by Audible's AI virtual voice; Recaps and Ask a Question widen in December. (Follow-up angle on the 11-17 Audible card - narrator impact.)

items.title: Just-in-Time Synthesis: A New Approach to an Old Genre
items.excerpt: Compares a commissioned review article with an AI-generated just-in-time overview answering the same reader need, asking how each is made and whether readers can trust it.

items.title: In France, the Publishing Industry Endures an Autumn of Discontent
items.excerpt: AI accusations against novelists Thelyson Orelien (denied) and Philippe Jaenada (who admitted slipping an AI-written sentence into his novel) dominate France's rentree, with suspicion disproportionately targeting authors of color.

items.title: The Worst Thing About AI Writing
items.excerpt: The Atlantic on France's AI literary scandal and how AI-authorship accusations fall hardest on Black writers. (Published time from outlet RSS; article page Cloudflare-gated.)

items.title: 'It's like the wild west': how AI has rocked the literary world
items.excerpt: With authors losing lucrative deals and writers removed from prize shortlists, accusations of AI use are sending shock waves through publishing.

items.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story
items.excerpt: After a month-long investigation the Caine Prize concluded Kundizeza's winning story The Blue Fighter was human-written.

items.title: New French literary prize will reward work created with AI help
items.excerpt: France's new Prix Pascal will reward books created with AI assistance, a first for French letters amid the season's AI-authorship rows.

items.title: A book club invited me to talk - it was an AI scam. Then it got weirder
items.excerpt: An author recounts being targeted by a fake book-club invitation run as an AI-powered scam aimed at writers. (Paywalled; title/date verified via reader proxy.)

items.title: Classic Novels Are Being Reduced To 30-Minute AI Audiobooks As Literature Faces a New Question
items.excerpt: Classic novels are being condensed into 30-minute AI audiobooks with cloned voices, raising questions about literary depth.

items.title: How 'I love You' becomes 'The moon is beautiful, isn't it?': The Craft of Translation and the limits of AI
items.excerpt: Manga translators and many U.S. publishers reject AI translation for missing nuance and visual context, while some Japanese companies push AI-assisted localization to speed releases.

items.title: AI firms turning books into toilet paper, committee told
items.excerpt: An Oireachtas committee heard AI companies are buying and destroying physical books to scan them for training data, as Irish writers press for copyright protections.

items.title: Farnham start-up aims to turn children's stories into books with Talebrix
items.excerpt: A Farnham couple is building Talebrix, a device that uses AI to turn children's spoken stories into personalised picture books.

items.title: Ghostwriters for celebrities like Dustin Hoffman are now selling points, not secrets. Is AI a factor?
items.excerpt: Once hidden, celebrity-memoir ghostwriters are now credited on covers; in an age of AI, a named human collaborator may signal authenticity.

items.title: The latest AI threat to books
items.excerpt: New Zealand ghostwriters of bestselling memoirs weigh AI's ability to draft book-length manuscripts as UK and US reports show AI already cutting ghostwriting commissions.

items.title: Not AI's to Take: arts, screen and media sectors join forces to protect creatives from AI theft
items.excerpt: 36 screen, media and literature organisations launch the Not AI's to Take campaign on 18 November demanding 'permission first and agreed payment' and no weakening of Australian copyright for AI firms.

items.title: Want to be a published writer? You might compete with an AI agent
items.excerpt: DePaul's urban essay magazine Slag Glass City grapples with a 'soulless' submission sent by an autonomous AI agent, prompting a rethink of its submission policy.

items.title: 투고가 쏟아진다…출판계도 AI 원고에 골머리
items.excerpt: 출판사 원고 투고가 작년 대비 40% 넘게 늘었고, 특히 에세이 분야에서 AI로 쓴 것으로 보이는 원고가 급증해 출판계가 검토 부담을 호소하고 있다.

items.title: 셀바스AI, AI 음성합성 기술 예스24 전자책에 적용·상용화
items.excerpt: 셀바스AI가 크로스링구얼 온디바이스 음성합성(TTS)을 예스24 ebook 앱에 적용해, 한국어 음색을 유지한 채 영어 문장까지 자연스럽게 읽어주는 기능을 상용화했다.

items.title: "AI가 읽고 책은 폐기" 캐나다 헌책방에 수상한 대량 주문
items.excerpt: AI 기업들이 학습 데이터용 중고 종이책을 대량 매입하면서 2022년 이전 출간본 몸값이 뛰고, 캐나다 중고 서점들이 책 파괴를 막기 위해 대량 주문을 거절하고 있다.

items.title: "AI가 사용하는 콘텐츠, 함께 비용 받아내자"…美 3000여 권리자 결속
items.excerpt: 미국 권리자 3000여 곳이 AI 콘텐츠 이용료 공동 징수에 나서 야후 스카웃과 첫 유료 계약을 맺었고, 한국 출판계도 AI 데이터 기업 5곳과 협약했다.

items.title: 책 분류부터 운반까지 로봇이 척척…AI 만난 출판산업, 물류혁신 가속
items.excerpt: 교보문고 파주 제2물류센터에서 AI 로봇과 자동화 설비가 하루 최대 30만 권의 책 분류·포장·운반을 처리하는 등 출판 물류의 AI 전환이 빨라지고 있다.

items.title: TN library case: Chennai publisher arrested over procuring AI-generated books
items.excerpt: Tamil Nadu's vigilance directorate (DVAC) arrested a Chennai publisher over the supply of AI-generated books to public libraries. (Follow-up to 11-16 card: qualifies as DVAC action.)
